doc_verification.detail: Reachability: page https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/distributed/update-collection-cluster loads (WebFetch domain-blocked, but MCP web-reader fetched both the rendered page and the .md rendering, and curl fetched the OpenAPI shards). Version: URL path v-1-18-x + page header v1.18.x vs target 1.18.0 -> major.minor matched. Endpoint precision: page documents POST /collections/{collection_name}/cluster with required path param collection_name and a oneOf wrapped-variant body (MoveShardOperation | ... | CreateShardingKeyOperation | ...) — exactly matches the contract endpoint_registry entry (path=cluster+collection+update, method=POST) and the requests in the log. Content consistency FAILS on the claim-critical clauses: the v1.18.x page's Response section documents ONLY '200 successful operation' — there is no documented 404-for-missing-collection and no documented 400-on-invalid-peer/shard on this page; the underlying official OpenAPI shards (api-reference.json / api-reference-2.json, path /collections/{collection_name}/cluster post.responses) likewise declare only the 200 response. The contract's '404 for a missing collection' clause (and the 400 clause) — the exact premise of this candidate's oracle EXPECT_STATUS=(404,) — is absent from the cited documentation; raw_knowledge.json nevertheless recorded behavioral '200 ok; 400 invalid peer/shard; 404 collection' and expected_responses {200,400,404} for this endpoint, i.e. those clauses entered the chain at raw-extraction time without support on the cited page or spec (doc_quote in endpoint_registry is likewise unsupported by the page text). The 200-face and the body schema (create_sharding_key requires shard_key; no shard_id field under create_sharding_key) ARE consistent with the documentation. Aggregate DOC_PARTIAL: endpoint identity/version/200-face verified; the 404/400 disposition clauses are documentation-unsupported.

http_semantics.note: A request-side-decidable error (malformed body: create_sharding_key missing required shard_key and carrying non-existent field shard_id) returned HTTP 400 with error envelope {"status":{"error":"Format error in JSON body: ..."}} — proper 4xx status usage, no 2xx+business-code masking. The status code is correct HTTP semantics for an unparseable body; the dispute is only whether a 404 should have won, which presupposes a parseable body.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 ok; 400 on an invalid peer/shard; 404 for a missing collection
contract_grounding.note: violates=false reasoning (per violates-declaration self-check, one of the two honest branches chosen explicitly): the observed parameter (collection_name=bccu1b16c0b44ghost1, a never-created name) IS inside the quote's constraint domain, but the observation never exercised the 'missing collection returns 404' branch because the request failed at a prior, name-independent validation layer — the actix JSON extractor rejected the body itself (missing required shard_key / unknown field shard_id under create_sharding_key), returning 400 for the existing-collection control identically. The 400 is therefore not evidence that the API mishandles a missing collection; it is correct format-error semantics for an unparseable body. Additionally, per cross-log 007 and source, even a well-formed body cannot reach the 404 branch on this deployment (consensus_state none -> 400 'Distributed mode disabled' precedes the existence check), and the 404 clause itself is absent from the cited v1.18.x page and OpenAPI spec (only 200 documented).

chain_trace.break_detail: Three links broken, first-in-order recorded as primary: (1) doc — the constraint's 404/400 clauses are absent from the cited v1.18.x page and its OpenAPI spec (Response documents only 200), so the oracle premise EXPECT_STATUS=(404,) has no documentation support on the cited source; (2) script — OP_BODY is schema-invalid (create_sharding_key without required shard_key, with non-member shard_id), and the in-log control (existing collection -> identical 400 'Format error in JSON body: data did not match any variant of untagged enum ClusterOperations') proves the 400 fires at JSON deserialization before any collection-name handling, so the expected-404-vs-got-400 comparison never tested the missing-collection branch; (3) log-verdict — the DEFECT_FOUND (Type2) line misattributes a body-format rejection to the collection-name face. Independently, cross-log boundary_cluster_collection_update_007 shows that even a well-formed create_sharding_key body gets 400 'Bad request: Distributed mode disabled' on this single-node deployment before the existence check, so the 404 branch is unreachable for ANY collection name in this environment.

The observed 400 originated at the FIRST layer (extractor), so neither the distributed-mode gate nor the existence check was ever reached; the collection name was never consulted.
source_grounding.outcome_note: The contract-required validation exists in source: the missing-collection 404 face is implemented (get_collection -> validate_collection_exists -> StorageError::NotFound -> 404 at src/actix/helpers.rs:246), and a body-format 400 face plus a distributed-mode 400 gate precede it in request order. The observed 400 is the body-format layer correctly rejecting the script's schema-invalid OP_BODY (create_sharding_key without required shard_key, with non-member shard_id), deterministically and name-independently — matching the in-log control (existing collection -> identical 400) and cross-log 007 (schema-valid body -> different business-layer 400 'Distributed mode disabled'). No explicit by-design annotation is involved (nothing was silently accepted or substituted).

excluded: concurrency race (all four requests are synchronous, sequential, and deterministic — identical 400 bodies within microseconds)
cache delay / state staleness (no state mutation is involved in a format-level rejection)
transport or environment outage (every request returned a well-formed HTTP 400 JSON envelope; /healthz never needed)
silent value substitution / default acceptance (nothing was accepted; the request was rejected — the Type2 claim itself concedes rejection)
surviving: request-construction error in the triggering script: OP_BODY {"create_sharding_key": {"shard_id": 4321}} is schema-invalid per both the v1.18.x documentation and the source enum (create_sharding_key requires shard_key; shard_id is not a member), so the 400 format error is attributable to the script's own body, not to the unknown collection name — proven by the in-log control on an existing collection returning the identical 400

environment limitation: single-node deployment (consensus_state none) returns 400 'Distributed mode disabled' for ANY well-formed cluster-update op before the collection-existence check, so the documented 404 branch is unreachable for any name in this environment (cross-log boundary_cluster_collection_update_007: schema-valid body -> 400 'Bad request: Distributed mode disabled'; that script self-verdicted SCRIPT_ERROR 'no acceptable carrier operation on this deployment')

contract over-claim: the 404-for-missing-collection clause (and the 400-on-invalid-peer/shard clause) asserted by qdrant_behavioral_cluster_collection_update_001 does not appear on the cited v1.18.x page or in its OpenAPI spec (Response documents only 200); the clauses originate from raw_knowledge.json's unsupported behavioral line, so the oracle premise EXPECT_STATUS=(404,) lacks documentation grounding
